To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are no first order transitions between the Fermi-liquid and Wigner crystalline phases in clean Si MOS devices; instead, the sequence of transitions is continuous, with a variety of intermediate liquid crystalline phases.

the Wigner crystal in a clean MOSFET is not a ground state, and that the ``metal-insulator'' transition is not a direct first order transition but rather a sequence of continuous phase transformations.

{\it (1) there can be no first order transition between the liquid and crystalline phases of a clean 2D electron system in a MOSFET; instead there must be a sequence of continuous phase transition between the liquid, the crystalline, and a variety of liquid crystalline phases; (2) the liquid crystal phase can be a nematic or smectic, depending on the geometry of the device and on the electron density.}
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the ground state of an interacting electron gas in the presence of a strong random potential.
the study of the electronic phase diagram of two-dimensional electron systems in the vicinity of the metal-insulator transition.
the nature of the phase transition between the liquid and crystal phases of a 2-dimensional electron fluid, and the nature of the intermediate liquid crystalline phases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two-dimensional electron gas does not undergo a first order transition from a Fermi liquid into a Wigner crystal, but rather a sequence of continuous transitions into a variety of liquid crystalline phases.
the two-dimensional electron gas is a liquid crystalline phase.
the Wigner crystal does {\it not} occur in the two dimensional electron gas in Si MOSFET's.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two dimensional electron gas in a Si MOSFET is a ``complex'' fluid.

the Wigner crystal phase in a clean MOSFET can be viewed as a {\it metastable} state, which is not the thermodynamic ground state of the system, but which can be trapped as a result of a kinetic barrier.
there is no first order transition between the Fermi Liquid phase and the Wigner Crystal in the two dimensional electron gas in a clean Si MOSFETS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Wigner crystal is not a good model for the insulating phase in the apparent metal-insulator transition in MOSFETs, since there are no first order phase transitions to a crystal phase in a clean system.

the physics of two-dimensional electronic systems is much more complex than has been previously appreciated, and that the ``metal to insulator transition,'' as currently conceived, is not a good description of the physics of the two-dimensional electron gas.

the electronic phase diagram of a clean MOSFET cannot be described in terms of the conventional Landau theory of phase transitions, which is based on the assumption that a single order parameter is sufficient to describe all of the relevant physics.
